by a long-tendril

only smudged fingerprints

sweep in, sweep out, sweep spray

Walter's love is earning him a quiet reward this New Year. Which is: Two affable friends will come to visit for the holidays. Lee has a little daughter, who is becoming her father's copy. Lee's name in Vietnamese means 'dragon.' His daughter, Hailey, is five, and is coming to us armed with a big personality. She will call you Nana. She will ask you to play the piano. She is every daughter this world can bear. If I ever had a child, I would want her child to be this.
I met her father in high school. That was years ago. It gave me chills to see Hailey fit the sum of a small life so nicely. It helped me recall my own first years into the world, when my mother would sit me up on her lap and give me bits of lamb, gtk on bowls, and rice.
The world is so little, yet there are endless roads we can travel. The love we endure is for the small story, which means we tend to outlive the longer ones.
Lee and I were friends then, I met him 25 years ago. It is close to an immeasurable amount of time, only what can be measured by your reflections or breaths. Imagine for a moment we're both reporters who say half the time don't know what will happen next. It happens too fast for a moment to be taken.
I only hope when you come to visit, you can bless me with a gift. Even if it is water.
